summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (MAC NE Story of Joseph/32)

data.turoyo: saləq li+goro, nqəḥle. Nqəḥle. Aṯi reḥe du…reḥe du+aḥuno.
data.translation: he went up to the roof, he sniffed. He sniffed. Along came the scent of… the scent of his brother.

rationale: Thin Preterit cell; absolute sniffing with separately introduced scent. Repetition quoted once, both tokens decided.

data.turoyo: Hano, u šer, annaqqa aṯi, nqəḥle bi ḥurma. Ḥurma yo, lə ggoyəš eba.
data.translation: Der Löwe kam heran, beschnüffelte die Frau, aber da es ja eine Frau war, tat er ihr nichts.

rationale: Thin Preterit cell; b-marked sniffed target instead of a direct smell noun.

data.turoyo: Hano šqile u ḥaṣo me Bagram, u səsyo ste nqəḥle reḥa di səsto w bəṯra w bəṯra.
data.translation: Unser Mann ritt hinter Bägräm her, sein hengstwitterte den Geruch der Stute und immer hinter ihr her!

rationale: Thin Preterit cell; animal perceiver with possessed smell object.

data.turoyo: Faqat nqəḥḥe reḥayna, innu d kətna ənsanat, me tamo ṣədde ruḥayye w aṯən, d həǧmilan, innu d qəṭlilan w d əxlilan.
data.translation: Aber sie witterten, daß wir Menschen waren, machten sich auf und kamen heran, um uns anzufallen, zu töten und zu fressen.

rationale: Brings Preterit to five; unusual plural nqəḥḥe and an identifying content clause.

summary: All 14 tokens fit inherited sense 1: sniffing, scent detection and inhaling. The already quoted hawa example supports breathing air without a new sense or idiom.
Preterit perceivers have l-agent morphology, including assimilated plural nqəḥḥe; Infectum has ordinary subject inflection. No distinct experiencer Preterit Intransitive construction is evidenced.
Scent can be a direct reḥo/reḥe NP; the sniffed entity/source can be b-marked (bi ḥurma, nqaḥ ebe). Sniffing also occurs without an expressed object, with scent introduced in a following clause.
Two repeated nqəḥle tokens in MAC NE Story of Joseph/32 are one example but retain separate decisions. The singular and plural Imperativ forms are directly attested.
52/27, 52/152, 73/64 and 73/100 are already quoted and are not duplicated. Infectum-wa 73/100 describes an unrealized smelling opportunity rather than establishing another sense.
No new collocation or etymological claim is justified by these passages.
The inherited etymology is already queried in the headword. Can the editors establish its relationship to Arabic nkh? The corpus here does not resolve it.
